quests.hint: This verb means to tell the difference between two similar things by examining them carefully.
quests.explanation: 'Distinguish between,' 'distinguish A from B,' and 'fail to distinguish' are key. 'Distinguishable' is the adjective. 'Distinguishing feature' is a key difference between things.
quests.textToSpeak: It is important to ___ between correlation and causation when analysing data.
quests.correctAnswer: It is important to distinguish between correlation and causation when analysing data.

quests.hint: This verb means to combine different elements into a single unified whole or conclusion.
quests.explanation: 'Synthesize information,' 'synthesize ideas,' and 'synthesize findings' are key. 'Synthesis' is the noun. In chemistry, it means to create a compound. Academically, it means to combine ideas.
quests.textToSpeak: The essay asks you to ___ multiple sources and draw your own overall conclusion.
quests.correctAnswer: The essay asks you to synthesize multiple sources and draw your own overall conclusion.

quests.hint: This verb means to express an amount or value as a number so it can be measured.
quests.explanation: 'Quantify the impact,' 'difficult to quantify,' and 'quantifiable results' are key. 'Quantitative' relates to numbers; 'qualitative' relates to descriptions. Both are research methods.
quests.textToSpeak: It is very difficult to ___ the emotional benefits of a strong community support network.
quests.correctAnswer: It is very difficult to quantify the emotional benefits of a strong community support network.

quests.hint: This verb means to give good reasons or evidence to support or explain a decision.
quests.explanation: 'Justify a decision,' 'justify your answer,' and 'hard to justify' are key. 'Justification' is the noun. 'Unjustified' means without adequate reason. 'Justified' means well-reasoned.
quests.textToSpeak: She was asked to ___ her decision to restructure the department at such short notice.
quests.correctAnswer: She was asked to justify her decision to restructure the department at such short notice.

quests.hint: This verb means to admit that something is true, even though you may not want to.
quests.explanation: 'Concede a point,' 'concede defeat,' and 'I concede that' are key. In debates, conceding a point shows intellectual honesty. 'Concession' is the noun: 'make a concession.'
quests.textToSpeak: In the debate, she was willing to ___ that the opposing argument had some merit.
quests.correctAnswer: In the debate, she was willing to concede that the opposing argument had some merit.

quests.hint: This verb means to state something that is the direct opposite of what another person has claimed.
quests.explanation: 'Contradict yourself,' 'contradict the evidence,' and 'contradiction' are key. 'Contradictory' is the adjective: 'contradictory statements.' 'Self-contradictory' means logically inconsistent.
quests.textToSpeak: The new evidence seemed to ___ the conclusions of every study that came before it.
quests.correctAnswer: The new evidence seemed to contradict the conclusions of every study that came before it.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something that is very common and found in many places.
quests.explanation: 'Prevalent issue,' 'increasingly prevalent,' and 'prevalent in' are key. 'Prevalence' is the noun: 'the prevalence of.' More formal than 'common' or 'widespread.'
quests.textToSpeak: Smartphone addiction has become remarkably ___ among young people in recent years.
quests.correctAnswer: Smartphone addiction has become remarkably prevalent among young people in recent years.

quests.hint: This adjective describes a system, plan, or approach that is complex and highly developed.
quests.explanation: 'Sophisticated analysis,' 'highly sophisticated,' and 'a sophisticated understanding' are key. 'Sophistication' is the noun. Can describe both people (worldly) and things (complex).
quests.textToSpeak: The new software uses a highly ___ algorithm to predict user behaviour and preferences.
quests.correctAnswer: The new software uses a highly sophisticated algorithm to predict user behaviour and preferences.

quests.hint: This verb means to give more detail, explanation, or examples about something you have said.
quests.explanation: 'Elaborate on that,' 'could you elaborate?' and 'elaborate further' are key. 'In more elaborate detail' means in greater depth. 'Elaborate' as an adjective means highly detailed.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you ___ on that last point? I did not quite follow your reasoning there.
quests.correctAnswer: Could you elaborate on that last point? I did not quite follow your reasoning there.

quests.hint: This verb means to strengthen or deepen an idea, habit, or skill by repeating it.
quests.explanation: 'Reinforce a message,' 'reinforce behaviour,' and 'positive reinforcement' are key. 'Reinforcement' is the noun. 'Negative reinforcement' is when removing something encourages behaviour.
quests.textToSpeak: Practising speaking every day will ___ your confidence and fluency over time.
quests.correctAnswer: Practising speaking every day will reinforce your confidence and fluency over time.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something that is stated or meant but not directly expressed.
quests.explanation: 'Implicit assumption,' 'implicit bias,' and 'implicitly understood' are key. 'Implicit' contrasts with 'explicit' (clearly stated). 'Implicitly' is the adverb form.
quests.textToSpeak: There was an ___ agreement between them that neither had to spell out in words.
quests.correctAnswer: There was an implicit agreement between them that neither had to spell out in words.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something that is stated clearly and directly - not implied.
quests.explanation: 'Explicit instructions,' 'make it explicit,' and 'explicitly stated' are key. 'Explicitly' is the adverb. 'Explicit content' means material that is clearly and directly described.
quests.textToSpeak: The contract contained very ___ clauses about what would happen in case of late delivery.
quests.correctAnswer: The contract contained very explicit clauses about what would happen in case of late delivery.

quests.hint: This noun refers to an earlier case or decision used as a guide for handling similar future cases.
quests.explanation: 'Set a precedent,' 'legal precedent,' and 'unprecedented' (no precedent) are key. 'Precedent-setting' describes something that creates a new standard for others to follow.
quests.textToSpeak: The court's ruling set an important ___ for how similar cases should be handled.
quests.correctAnswer: The court's ruling set an important precedent for how similar cases should be handled.

quests.hint: This verb means to gradually make something weaker or less effective from below.
quests.explanation: 'Undermine confidence,' 'undermine authority,' and 'completely undermine' are key. Originally meant to dig under a wall to collapse it. Now used figuratively for any gradual weakening.
quests.textToSpeak: His constant criticism of her work began to seriously ___ her self-confidence.
quests.correctAnswer: His constant criticism of her work began to seriously undermine her self-confidence.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the association or feeling that a word carries beyond its literal meaning.
quests.explanation: 'Negative connotation,' 'positive connotation,' and 'the word carries connotations of' are key. 'Denotation' is the literal meaning; 'connotation' is the implied emotional meaning.
quests.textToSpeak: The word 'slim' has a positive ___ while 'thin' can sometimes sound negative or unhealthy.
quests.correctAnswer: The word 'slim' has a positive connotation while 'thin' can sometimes sound negative or unhealthy.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a comparison that helps explain something by relating it to something familiar.
quests.explanation: 'An apt metaphor,' 'use a metaphor,' and 'extend the metaphor' are key. A metaphor says X IS Y; a simile says X is LIKE Y. Metaphors make abstract ideas more vivid.
quests.textToSpeak: She used the ___ of a marathon to describe the long and tiring journey to recovery.
quests.correctAnswer: She used the metaphor of a marathon to describe the long and tiring journey to recovery.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a contrast created by placing two very different things side by side.
quests.explanation: 'Sharp juxtaposition,' 'in juxtaposition with,' and 'create a juxtaposition' are key. 'Juxtapose' is the verb. Juxtaposition is a powerful rhetorical and literary technique.
quests.textToSpeak: The documentary creates a striking ___ between extreme wealth and grinding poverty.
quests.correctAnswer: The documentary creates a striking juxtaposition between extreme wealth and grinding poverty.

quests.hint: This noun refers to an indirect reference to another literary work, event, or idea.
quests.explanation: 'Make an allusion,' 'literary allusion,' and 'allusion to' are key. 'Allude to' is the verb: 'she alluded to the earlier incident.' An allusion assumes the audience will recognise it.
quests.textToSpeak: The poem contains a clear ___ to Milton's Paradise Lost in its final stanza.
quests.correctAnswer: The poem contains a clear allusion to Milton's Paradise Lost in its final stanza.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the use of humorous or exaggerated language to criticize something.
quests.explanation: 'Political satire,' 'biting satire,' and 'satirize' are key. 'Satirical' is the adjective. Satire mocks its subject in order to expose its flaws. Closely related to irony.
quests.textToSpeak: The novel is a sharp ___ of the political system that made many people uncomfortable.
quests.correctAnswer: The novel is a sharp satire of the political system that made many people uncomfortable.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the use of words that mean the opposite of what you actually mean.
quests.explanation: 'Verbal irony,' 'dramatic irony,' and 'a sense of irony' are key. 'Ironic' is the adjective. 'Ironically' introduces a surprising contradiction. 'Heavy irony' means very obvious sarcasm.
quests.textToSpeak: She said 'what a lovely day' with clear ___, given the torrential rain outside.
quests.correctAnswer: She said 'what a lovely day' with clear irony, given the torrential rain outside.

quests.hint: This adjective describes language or reasoning that is expressed clearly and is easy to understand.
quests.explanation: 'Lucid explanation,' 'lucid writing,' and 'remarkably lucid' are key. 'Lucidity' is the noun. 'Lucid' can also describe someone who is conscious and thinking clearly: 'a lucid moment.'
quests.textToSpeak: Despite the complexity of the topic, his lecture was remarkably ___ and easy to follow.
quests.correctAnswer: Despite the complexity of the topic, his lecture was remarkably lucid and easy to follow.

quests.hint: This verb means to use something to maximum advantage for your own benefit.
quests.explanation: 'Leverage your skills,' 'leverage technology,' and 'leverage a position' are key. 'Leverage' is also a noun: 'have leverage over.' Originally a physics term; now widely used in business.
quests.textToSpeak: She knew how to ___ her network to secure the funding needed for the project.
quests.correctAnswer: She knew how to leverage her network to secure the funding needed for the project.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something that is not tangible - existing as a quality or feeling.
quests.explanation: 'Intangible benefits,' 'intangible assets,' and 'hard to measure, intangible value' are key. 'Tangible' means physical and measurable. 'Intangibles' in business include brand value.
quests.textToSpeak: Trust and loyalty are ___ benefits of good leadership that cannot easily be measured.
quests.correctAnswer: Trust and loyalty are intangible benefits of good leadership that cannot easily be measured.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something real, clear, and able to be directly experienced.
quests.explanation: 'Tangible result,' 'tangible evidence,' and 'tangible benefit' are key. 'Tangibly' is the adverb. 'Tangible progress' means visible, measurable improvement. Opposite of 'intangible.'
quests.textToSpeak: After six months of work, they finally had ___ results to show the investors.
quests.correctAnswer: After six months of work, they finally had tangible results to show the investors.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something that is deeply significant or key to a major change.
quests.explanation: 'Pivotal moment,' 'pivotal role,' and 'a pivotal decision' are key. More dramatic than 'important' or 'crucial.' 'Pivot point' is related - a moment when everything changes direction.
quests.textToSpeak: That meeting turned out to be a truly ___ moment in the history of the organisation.
quests.correctAnswer: That meeting turned out to be a truly pivotal moment in the history of the organisation.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something that has never happened or existed before in history.
quests.explanation: 'Unprecedented situation,' 'unprecedented growth,' and 'an unprecedented level of' are key. 'Precedent' means a past example; 'unprecedented' means no past example exists.
quests.textToSpeak: The scale of the challenge was truly ___ - nothing like this had ever occurred before.
quests.correctAnswer: The scale of the challenge was truly unprecedented - nothing like this had ever occurred before.

quests.hint: This adjective describes a piece of work that is extremely important and highly influential.
quests.explanation: 'Seminal work,' 'seminal study,' and 'a seminal contribution' are key. 'Seminal' originally meant of seeds - now means foundational in a field. Stronger than 'important' or 'influential.'
quests.textToSpeak: Darwin's On the Origin of Species is considered the most ___ scientific text of its era.
quests.correctAnswer: Darwin's On the Origin of Species is considered the most seminal scientific text of its era.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a situation that contains two contradictory things that are both true.
quests.explanation: 'A paradox,' 'seemingly a paradox,' and 'the paradox of' are key. 'Paradoxical' is the adjective. 'Paradoxically' introduces a surprising statement that seems contradictory.
quests.textToSpeak: It is something of a ___ that working fewer hours can sometimes increase overall output.
quests.correctAnswer: It is something of a paradox that working fewer hours can sometimes increase overall output.

quests.hint: This verb means to bring two opposing ideas or people into agreement or harmony.
quests.explanation: 'Reconcile differences,' 'reconcile accounts,' and 'difficult to reconcile' are key. 'Reconciliation' is the noun. 'Irreconcilable differences' means they cannot be resolved.
quests.textToSpeak: It is hard to ___ her public statements with her private actions on the matter.
quests.correctAnswer: It is hard to reconcile her public statements with her private actions on the matter.

quests.hint: This adjective describes a feature that is naturally part of something and cannot be removed.
quests.explanation: 'Inherent risk,' 'inherent value,' and 'inherently difficult' are key. 'Inherent' is similar to 'intrinsic.' 'Inherently' is the adverb: 'it is inherently complicated.'
quests.textToSpeak: There is an ___ tension between speed and quality that all designers must navigate.
quests.correctAnswer: There is an inherent tension between speed and quality that all designers must navigate.
